## 2. MRT API inventory (Task 1)

The storefront consumes SFCC through the MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/api`, base host `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` (Dev: shortCode `qmyt7hks`, org `f_ecom_bkzk_002`, site `ZimmermannAU`). Authentication is **SLAS private-client** (guest and registered tokens; the client secret is held server-side). Requests and responses are JSON over TLS.

APIs relevant to product, category, and pricing:

| API family | Path root | Data served | Verbs | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shopper Products | `/product/shopper-products/v1/*` | Product detail (master/variant, images), **price** (`priceRanges` per pricebook), and the **category tree** (`getCategory`) | GET | SLAS |
| Shopper Search | `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category product listing (`cgid` refinement), keyword search, faceting, sort | GET | SLAS |
| Shopper Login (SLAS) | `/shopper/auth/v1/*` (`oauth2` token and JWKS) | Guest and registered auth; the enabler for every read above | GET, POST | n/a |

**Payload conventions.** The storefront pulls related data in one call with `expand` (e.g. `expand=prices,promotions,variations,images`) and `perPricebook=true` for pricebook-aware pricing. Promotions surface as `productPromotions` (a `calloutMsg`, and a `promotionalPrice` at the variant level).

**Out of scope** (other problems, documented elsewhere): cart and checkout (Shopper Baskets, Shopper Orders), account and wishlist (Shopper Customers), personalization (Shopper Context, Einstein), OCAPI (configured but not called by app code), MuleSoft direct reads, and the Managed Runtime Admin API.

---

## 3. What can serve product, category, and pricing now (Task 2)

Verified by a local PWA run against dev `bkzk-002` (23-24 Jul 2026), SCAPI network traffic captured:

| Capability | API | Verified result |
|---|---|---|

| Category listing / search | Shopper Search | `product-search?refine=cgid=clothing` returns 200 (`total: 1`) |

| Price | Shopper Products (`expand=prices`, `perPricebook`) | 625 AUD from pricebook `au-aud-list-prices` |
| Discount / strikethrough | promotions via `expand=promotions` | 10% promo returns `promotionalPrice` 562.50 at variant level; PDP renders A$562.50 against a struck A$625 |
| Inventory | on the product record | `inventory_m_au`, ats 10, orderable |
| Auth | SLAS | guest token issued and accepted |

**Conclusion:** SCAPI serves product, category, pricing, and promotional pricing in dev today, and the storefront renders them with **no code change**. Consumption is not the blocker.

---

## 4. Current data state and how it is populated

- **Dev `bkzk-002` (verified 23-24 Jul).** Categories, pricebooks, and inventory are configured; one sample product (`4673TS251`) is present, priced and in stock with a working promotion. Business Manager first-time setup (storefront-catalogue assignment, search-index rebuild) is done. Building this feed is SFCC-121's scope.

*Loading-mechanism sources: Confluence Business Manager Configuration Management (309657601) and the Catalogue Sync pages (312508418, 315490342). Whether a documented `data/sample` bulk-import set exists for the sandbox is unconfirmed (open item).*

---

## 5. Limitations and gaps (Task 3)

- **Other sites and tiers unconfirmed.** Only `ZimmermannAU` on dev is verified; other storefronts and non-dev tiers are not checked.
- **Permanent feed pending.** The AP21 data feed to SFCC is not built; SFCC-121 (Validate MuleSoft Sync Process) is In Progress.

---

## 6. Permanent vs workaround (Task 4)

| Element | Classification |
|---|---|
| SCAPI-via-MRT for product/category/pricing consumption | **Permanent** (the storefront's supported model; no code change needed) |
| SLAS private-client auth via MRT | **Permanent** |
| AP21 data feed to SFCC (catalogue via MuleSoft; price as file-based Pricebook XML, delivery path TBC) | **Permanent** (data population; not yet built) |
| Manual Business Manager creation of sample data | **Workaround** (interim only; throwaway once the feed delivers) |
| OCAPI via MRT | Configured fallback; currently unused |

- A broader sample-data set for front-end testing (multiple styles across categories).

=== 01-sfcc.md: full SCAPI endpoint inventory table ===
All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single domain and share one SFCC realm.

- **The refresh-token cookie is shared across storefronts.** Every storefront lives on the same domain, so the `httpOnly` cookie is sent on every path prefix. No cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A token issued for `zimm-au` is not valid for `zimm-uk` — this is a hard SLAS platform constraint. On a storefront switch the SSR layer performs a fresh authorisation for the destination channel using the SLAS Trusted System on Behalf (TSOB) flow: it calls `getTrustedSystemAccessToken` with the shopper's `login_id`, which issues a new channel-scoped token server-side without prompting the customer. A registered shopper stays signed in transparently. A guest session does not carry over — guest tokens and baskets are site-scoped. **TSOB rate limit:** SLAS returns HTTP 409 if multiple TSOB calls are made for the same shopper within a 3-second window — the SSR layer must not fire duplicate TSOB calls on rapid storefront switches (debounce or dedupe at the MRT layer).
- **Baskets do not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency. Switching storefront starts a fresh basket; carrying one across a currency boundary would produce wrong prices.
- **Checkout handoff is a separate boundary.** When handing off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into Global-e's hosted checkout.

## 4. Data exchanged

| Resource                           | Verbs                    | Notes                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | GET, POST                | SLAS authentication and token lifecycle                                                                                                         |
| `/product/shopper-products/v1/*`   | GET                      | Product details, master/variant resolution                                                                                                      |
| `/search/shopper-search/v1/*`      | GET                      | Catalogue search, faceting, sort, suggestions                                                                                                   |
| `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*`   | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Basket lifecycle, line items, shipments, payment instruments                                                                                    |
| `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*`    | POST, GET                | Order placement and lookup (SFCC-owned checkouts only)                                                                                          |
| `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | GET, POST, PATCH         | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references                                                                                                    |
| `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | GET                      | Active promotions, coupon validation                                                                                                            |
| Einstein recommendations endpoints | GET                      | Personalised recommendations slot. Consent-gated (Didomi purpose TBC) — falls back to a static SFCC merchandising group if consent is not given |

Every request carries the site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and SLAS bearer token. PII travels over TLS only. PCI scope is Adyen's — SFCC holds token references only.

## 5. reCAPTCHA on register and login (CRM-008)

- The storefront loads the reCAPTCHA v3 script on register and login forms only — not on any other page — and only after the customer first touches the form, so the script never blocks first paint.
- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
- reCAPTCHA loads on form interaction regardless of consent. **Exception: EU and UK** — in those regions it only loads after Didomi consent, which means a visitor who declines gets no bot protection there.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

# SFCC MRT API Capabilities: Spike Findings (SFCC-122)

> **Draft for squad review.** SFCC-122 spike deliverable: a documented inventory of the SFCC APIs available through MRT for product, category, and pricing consumption, and what can be built and tested in the lower environments before the AP21/MuleSoft feed is ready.

| | |
|---|---|
| Jira | SFCC-122 (Spike, Squad-A; epic SFCC-1 Platform Setup) |
| Author | Angelo Navarro, Squad-A / FED Lead |
| Status | Draft, for review |
| Verified against | dev sandbox `bkzk-002`, local PWA run, 23-24 Jul 2026 |

---

## 1. Summary

- **What "MRT API" means here.** Managed Runtime is the PWA Kit hosting/proxy layer. Product, category, and pricing data are served by **SCAPI (Salesforce Commerce API, the Shopper APIs)**, reached through the MRT proxy (`/mobify/proxy/api`). The separate Managed Runtime Admin API is platform / CI-CD and out of scope.
- **The APIs are ready; data was the gap.** SCAPI can serve product, category, and pricing today. At spike outset the sandbox had no data because the AP21-to-SFCC feed is not built yet.
- **Dev is now seeded and verified.** `bkzk-002` has categories, pricebooks, inventory, and one sample product (priced, in stock, with a working promotion strikethrough), all consumable via SCAPI with no app-code change.
- **Interim data is manual; scale and real data need AP21.** The current sample was hand-created in Business Manager; broader and real data depend on the permanent AP21 data feed to SFCC (SFCC-121).

---

## 2. MRT API inventory (Task 1)

The storefront consumes SFCC through the MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/api`, base host `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` (Dev: shortCode `qmyt7hks`, org `f_ecom_bkzk_002`, site `ZimmermannAU`). | API family | Path root | Data served | Verbs | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shopper Products | `/product/shopper-products/v1/*` | Product detail (master/variant, images), **price** (`priceRanges` per pricebook), and the **category tree** (`getCategory`) | GET | SLAS |
| Shopper Search | `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category product listing (`cgid` refinement), keyword search, faceting, sort | GET | SLAS |
| Shopper Login (SLAS) | `/shopper/auth/v1/*` (`oauth2` token and JWKS) | Guest and registered auth; the enabler for every read above | GET, POST | n/a |

| Inventory | on the product record | `inventory_m_au`, ats 10, orderable |

# SFCC MRT API Capabilities: Spike Findings (SFCC-122)

> **Draft for squad review.** SFCC-122 spike deliverable: a documented inventory of the SFCC APIs available through MRT for product, category, and pricing consumption, and what can be built and tested in the lower environments before the AP21/MuleSoft feed is ready.

| | |
|---|---|
| Jira | SFCC-122 (Spike, Squad-A; epic SFCC-1 Platform Setup) |
| Author | Angelo Navarro, Squad-A / FED Lead |
| Status | Draft, for review |
| Verified against | dev sandbox `bkzk-002`, local PWA run, 23-24 Jul 2026 |

---

## 1. Summary

- **What "MRT API" means here.** Managed Runtime is the PWA Kit hosting/proxy layer. Product, category, and pricing data are served by **SCAPI (Salesforce Commerce API, the Shopper APIs)**, reached through the MRT proxy (`/mobify/proxy/api`). The separate Managed Runtime Admin API is platform / CI-CD and out of scope.
- **The APIs are ready; data was the gap.** SCAPI can serve product, category, and pricing today. At spike outset the sandbox had no data because the AP21-to-SFCC feed is not built yet.
- **Dev is now seeded and verified.** `bkzk-002` has categories, pricebooks, inventory, and manually-created sample products with varied configurations (priced, in stock, with a working promotion strikethrough), all consumable via SCAPI with no app-code change.
- **Interim data is manual; scale and real data need AP21.** The current sample set was hand-created in Business Manager and continues to be added manually; full-catalogue and real data depend on the permanent AP21 data feed to SFCC (SFCC-121).

---

## 2. MRT API inventory (Task 1)

The storefront consumes SFCC through the MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/api`, base host `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` (Dev: shortCode `qmyt7hks`, org `f_ecom_bkzk_002`, site `ZimmermannAU`). Authentication is **SLAS private-client** (guest and registered tokens; the client secret is held server-side). Requests and responses are JSON over TLS.

APIs relevant to product, category, and pricing:

| API family | Path root | Data served | Verbs | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shopper Products | `/product/shopper-products/v1/*` | Product detail (master/variant, images), **price** (`priceRanges` per pricebook), and the **category tree** (`getCategory`) | GET | SLAS |
| Shopper Search | `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category product listing (`cgid` refinement), keyword search, faceting, sort | GET | SLAS |
| Shopper Login (SLAS) | `/shopper/auth/v1/*` (`oauth2` token and JWKS) | Guest and registered auth; the enabler for every read above | GET, POST | n/a |

**Payload conventions.** The storefront pulls related data in one call with `expand` (e.g. `expand=prices,promotions,variations,images`) and `perPricebook=true` for pricebook-aware pricing. Promotions surface as `productPromotions` (a `calloutMsg`, and a `promotionalPrice` at the variant level).

**Out of scope** (other problems, documented elsewhere): cart and checkout (Shopper Baskets, Shopper Orders), account and wishlist (Shopper Customers), personalization (Shopper Context, Einstein), OCAPI (configured but not called by app code), MuleSoft direct reads, and the Managed Runtime Admin API.

---

## 3. What can serve product, category, and pricing now (Task 2)

Verified by a local PWA run against dev `bkzk-002` (23-24 Jul 2026), SCAPI network traffic captured:

| Capability | API | Verified result |
|---|---|---|
| Category tree | Shopper Products `getCategory` | `clothing` and `new-arrivals` return 200; navigable |
| Category listing / search | Shopper Search | `product-search?refine=cgid=<category>` returns 200 with product hits |
| Product detail | Shopper Products | `4673TS251` returns 200 with attributes, images, variants |
| Price | Shopper Products (`expand=prices`, `perPricebook`) | 625 AUD from pricebook `au-aud-list-prices` |
| Discount / strikethrough | promotions via `expand=promotions` | 10% promo returns `promotionalPrice` 562.50 at variant level; PDP renders A$562.50 against a struck A$625 |
| Inventory | on the product record | `inventory_m_au`, ats 10, orderable |
| Auth | SLAS | guest token issued and accepted |

**Conclusion:** SCAPI serves product, category, pricing, and promotional pricing in dev today, and the storefront renders them with **no code change**. Consumption is not the blocker.

---

## 4. Current data state and how it is populated

- **Dev `bkzk-002` (verified 23-24 Jul).** Categories, pricebooks, and inventory are configured; one sample product (`4673TS251`) is present, priced and in stock with a working promotion. Business Manager first-time setup (storefront-catalogue assignment, search-index rebuild) is done. IDs in use: master catalogue `zimmermann-catalog`, storefront catalogues `zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog`, pricebooks `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`), inventory list `inventory_m_au`.
- **Interim (now).** Sample data is **created manually in Business Manager** by platform, because there is no AP21-to-SFCC integration yet. Additional sample data is also manual.
- **Permanent.** Product and catalogue land via the **AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC** feed. Price lands as file-based **Pricebook XML from AP21** (there is no pricebook write API, so price is always file-based); the exact delivery path (SFTP, API, or MuleSoft) is not yet confirmed (TSD Price, open item). Building this feed is SFCC-121's scope.

*Loading-mechanism sources: Confluence Business Manager Configuration Management (309657601) and the Catalogue Sync pages (312508418, 315490342). Whether a documented `data/sample` bulk-import set exists for the sandbox is unconfirmed (open item).*

---

## 5. Limitations and gaps (Task 3)

To be covered by AP21/MuleSoft (SFCC-121) or platform:

- **Data breadth.** Dev has a single hand-made style, not enough for scale, faceting, or listing tests. More requires manual creation until the feed exists.
- **Product attributes not final.** The attribute model is still under discussion (per Victor); attribute-bound PDP/PLP work may need rework.
- **Sale-pricebook path unexercised.** Discount display is verified via a **promotion**; the sale-pricebook ("was/now") path is a separate mechanism and has not been tested. (The sale strategy, promotion vs sale pricebook, is itself an open item in TSD Price.)
- **Other sites and tiers unconfirmed.** Only `ZimmermannAU` on dev is verified; other storefronts and non-dev tiers are not checked.
- **Permanent feed pending.** The AP21 data feed to SFCC is not built; SFCC-121 (Validate MuleSoft Sync Process) is In Progress.

---

## 6. Permanent vs workaround (Task 4)

| Element | Classification |
|---|---|
| SCAPI-via-MRT for product/category/pricing consumption | **Permanent** (the storefront's supported model; no code change needed) |
| SLAS private-client auth via MRT | **Permanent** |
| AP21 data feed to SFCC (catalogue via MuleSoft; price as file-based Pricebook XML, delivery path TBC) | **Permanent** (data population; not yet built) |
| Manual Business Manager creation of sample data | **Workaround** (interim only; throwaway once the feed delivers) |
| OCAPI via MRT | Configured fallback; currently unused |

---

## 7. Open items and follow-ups (owner: Victor / platform)

- A broader sample-data set for front-end testing (multiple styles across categories).
- Whether the documented `data/sample` import works against `bkzk-002` (would enable a bulk load instead of manual creation).
- Product-attribute model finalisation.
- The sale-pricebook ("was/now") path, if production markdowns are modelled as pricebooks rather than promotions.
- Per-site and per-tier seeding beyond AU/dev.
- Timeline for the permanent AP21 data feed to SFCC (SFCC-121).

- Jira (project SFCC): SFCC-122, SFCC-121 (Validate MuleSoft Sync Process), SFCC-1 (Platform Setup & Environments).
- Verification: local PWA run against dev `bkzk-002`, SCAPI network capture, 23-24 Jul 2026.
- Victor Crisostomo: sandbox and follow-up answers (23-24 Jul 2026).

- 27 Jul 2026: Reshaped from the earlier TSD-formatted draft into a spike findings / inventory doc, per review feedback (a spike needs findings, not a problem/options/decision TSD; removed PWA-implementation detail that overlapped the PWA TSD). **Payload conventions.** The storefront pulls related data in one call with `expand` (e.g. `expand=prices,promotions,variations,images`) and `perPricebook=true` for pricebook-aware pricing. Promotions surface as `productPromotions` (a `calloutMsg`, and a `promotionalPrice` at the variant level).

**Out of scope** (other problems, documented elsewhere): cart and checkout (Shopper Baskets, Shopper Orders), account and wishlist (Shopper Customers), personalization (Shopper Context, Einstein), OCAPI (configured but not called by app code), MuleSoft direct reads, and the Managed Runtime Admin API.

## 3. What can serve product, category, and pricing now (Task 2)

Verified by a local PWA run against dev `bkzk-002` (23-24 Jul 2026), SCAPI network traffic captured:

| Capability | API | Verified result |
|---|---|---|
| Category tree | Shopper Products `getCategory` | `clothing` and `new-arrivals` return 200; navigable |
| Category listing / search | Shopper Search | `product-search?refine=cgid=<category>` returns 200 with product hits |
| Product detail | Shopper Products | `4673TS251` returns 200 with attributes, images, variants |
| Price | Shopper Products (`expand=prices`, `perPricebook`) | 625 AUD from pricebook `au-aud-list-prices` |
| Discount / strikethrough | promotions via `expand=promotions` | 10% promo returns `promotionalPrice` 562.50 at variant level; PDP renders A$562.50 against a struck A$625 |
| Inventory | on the product record | `inventory_m_au`, ats 10, orderable |
| Auth | SLAS | guest token issued and accepted |

**Conclusion:** SCAPI serves product, category, pricing, and promotional pricing in dev today, and the storefront renders them with **no code change**. Consumption is not the blocker.

---

- **Dev `bkzk-002`.** Categories, pricebooks, and inventory are configured; a manually-created set of sample products with varied configurations is present, priced and in stock with a working promotion. Business Manager first-time setup (storefront-catalogue assignment, search-index rebuild) is done. IDs in use: master catalogue `zimmermann-catalog`, storefront catalogues `zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog`, pricebooks `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`), inventory list `inventory_m_au`.

## Why it's unaffected
An item with several colours/sizes is a **variation master with variation attributes + multiple variants**. SCAPI serves that through the *exact same* endpoints and parameters already documented — nothing new is unlocked:
- `getProduct` (Shopper Products) with **`expand=variations`** and **`allVariationProperties=true`** returns `variationAttributes` (the colour/size axes), the `variants` array, per-variant price (`perPricebook`), per-variant inventory, and per-variant promotions.

- The verified example (`4673TS251`) was itself a **master with 6 variants**, queried with `htype=master` + full variation properties — so the variation dimension is already exercised.

So whether a product has 1 option or 5 colours × 4 sizes, it's the same call, same auth, same payload shape. **§2 (Task 1) and §3's core answer (Task 2 = which APIs serve the data) don't change.**

## The honest nuance
What more multi-option products *would* add is **stronger verification**, not new capability — proof that multi-axis resolution (colour + size), per-variant price/inventory, and colour-specific image groups all render correctly. That matters because variation data is exactly the **data-sensitive** area where the earlier `allVariationProperties=true` **500s** showed up. A well-formed multi-colour product returning 200 is good evidence the variation path works *when the data is clean* — but that's evidence/data-state, not an inventory change.

## Recommendation
**No change needed to §3** — the capability is already proven and already worded to cover variants.

If you'd like the doc to *explicitly* assert "multi-option variation resolution (colour/size, per-variant price + inventory) verified," that's a one-line strengthening — but per your verify-with-source rule I'd only add it backed by a capture of a multi-colour product's `getProduct` showing `variationAttributes` with >1 axis. - **Interim data is manual; scale and real data need AP21.** The current sample set was hand-created in Business Manager and continues to be added manually; full-catalogue and real data depend on the permanent AP21 data feed to SFCC (SFCC-121).

---

## 2. MRT API inventory (Task 1)

| Shopper Search | `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category product listing (`cgid` refinement), keyword search, faceting, sort | GET | SLAS |

**Out of scope** (other problems, documented elsewhere): cart and checkout (Shopper Baskets, Shopper Orders), account and wishlist (Shopper Customers), personalization (Shopper Context, Einstein), OCAPI (configured but not called by app code), MuleSoft direct reads, and the Managed Runtime Admin API.

---

## 3. What can serve product, category, and pricing now (Task 2)

Verified by a local PWA run against dev `bkzk-002` (23-24 Jul 2026), SCAPI network traffic captured:

| Capability | API | Verified result |
|---|---|---|
| Category tree | Shopper Products `getCategory` | `clothing` and `new-arrivals` return 200; navigable |
| Category listing / search | Shopper Search | `product-search?refine=cgid=<category>` returns 200 with product hits |
| Product detail | Shopper Products | `4673TS251` returns 200 with attributes, images, variants |
| Price | Shopper Products (`expand=prices`, `perPricebook`) | 625 AUD from pricebook `au-aud-list-prices` |
| Discount / strikethrough | promotions via `expand=promotions` | 10% promo returns `promotionalPrice` 562.50 at variant level; PDP renders A$562.50 against a struck A$625 |
| Inventory | on the product record | `inventory_m_au`, ats 10, orderable |
| Auth | SLAS | guest token issued and accepted |

**Conclusion:** SCAPI serves product, category, pricing, and promotional pricing in dev today, and the storefront renders them with **no code change**. Consumption is not the blocker.

---

## 4. Current data state and how it is populated

- **Dev `bkzk-002`.** Categories, pricebooks, and inventory are configured; a manually-created set of sample products with varied configurations is present, priced and in stock with a working promotion. Business Manager first-time setup (storefront-catalogue assignment, search-index rebuild) is done. Building this feed is SFCC-121's scope.

---

| SCAPI-via-MRT for product/category/pricing consumption | **Permanent** (the storefront's supported model; no code change needed) |

input.content:
> **Draft for squad review.** SFCC-122 spike deliverable: a documented inventory of the SFCC APIs available through MRT for product, category, and pricing consumption, and what can be built and tested in the lower environments before the AP21/MuleSoft feed is ready.

| | |
|---|---|
| Jira | SFCC-122 (Spike, Squad-A; epic SFCC-1 Platform Setup) |
| Author | Angelo Navarro, Squad-A / FED Lead |
| Status | Draft, for review |
| Verified against | dev sandbox `bkzk-002`, local PWA run, 23-24 Jul 2026 |

---

## 1. Summary

- **What "MRT API" means here.** Managed Runtime is the PWA Kit hosting/proxy layer. Product, category, and pricing data are served by **SCAPI (Salesforce Commerce API, the Shopper APIs)**, reached through the MRT proxy (`/mobify/proxy/api`). The separate Managed Runtime Admin API is platform / CI-CD and out of scope.
- **The APIs are ready; data was the gap.** SCAPI can serve product, category, and pricing today. At spike outset the sandbox had no data because the AP21-to-SFCC feed is not built yet.
- **Dev is now seeded and verified.** `bkzk-002` has categories, pricebooks, inventory, and manually-created sample products with varied configurations (priced, in stock, with a working promotion strikethrough), all consumable via SCAPI with no app-code change.
- **Interim data is manual; scale and real data need AP21.** The current sample set was hand-created in Business Manager and continues to be added manually; full-catalogue and real data depend on the permanent AP21 data feed to SFCC (SFCC-121).

---

## 2. MRT API inventory (Task 1)

The storefront consumes SFCC through the MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/api`, base host `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` (Dev: shortCode `qmyt7hks`, org `f_ecom_bkzk_002`, site `ZimmermannAU`). Authentication is **SLAS private-client** (guest and registered tokens; the client secret is held server-side). Requests and responses are JSON over TLS.

APIs relevant to product, category, and pricing:

| API family | Path root | Data served | Verbs | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shopper Products | `/product/shopper-products/v1/*` | Product detail (master/variant, images), **price** (`priceRanges` per pricebook), and the **category tree** (`getCategory`) | GET | SLAS |
| Shopper Search | `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category product listing (`cgid` refinement), keyword search, faceting, sort | GET | SLAS |
| Shopper Login (SLAS) | `/shopper/auth/v1/*` (`oauth2` token and JWKS) | Guest and registered auth; the enabler for every read above | GET, POST | n/a |

**Payload conventions.** The storefront pulls related data in one call with `expand` (e.g. `expand=prices,promotions,variations,images`) and `perPricebook=true` for pricebook-aware pricing. Promotions surface as `productPromotions` (a `calloutMsg`, and a `promotionalPrice` at the variant level).

**Out of scope** (other problems, documented elsewhere): cart and checkout (Shopper Baskets, Shopper Orders), account and wishlist (Shopper Customers), personalization (Shopper Context, Einstein), OCAPI (configured but not called by app code), MuleSoft direct reads, and the Managed Runtime Admin API.

---

## 3. What can serve product, category, and pricing now (Task 2)

Verified by a local PWA run against dev `bkzk-002` (23-24 Jul 2026), SCAPI network traffic captured:

| Capability | API | Verified result |
|---|---|---|
| Category tree | Shopper Products `getCategory` | `clothing` and `new-arrivals` return 200; navigable |
| Category listing / search | Shopper Search | `product-search?refine=cgid=<category>` returns 200 with product hits |
| Product detail | Shopper Products | `4673TS251` returns 200 with attributes, images, variants |
| Price | Shopper Products (`expand=prices`, `perPricebook`) | 625 AUD from pricebook `au-aud-list-prices` |
| Discount / strikethrough | promotions via `expand=promotions` | 10% promo returns `promotionalPrice` 562.50 at variant level; PDP renders A$562.50 against a struck A$625 |
| Inventory | on the product record | `inventory_m_au`, ats 10, orderable |
| Auth | SLAS | guest token issued and accepted |

**Conclusion:** SCAPI serves product, category, pricing, and promotional pricing in dev today, and the storefront renders them with **no code change**. Consumption is not the blocker.

---

## 4. Current data state and how it is populated

- **Dev `bkzk-002`.** Categories, pricebooks, and inventory are configured; a manually-created set of sample products with varied configurations is present, priced and in stock with a working promotion. Business Manager first-time setup (storefront-catalogue assignment, search-index rebuild) is done. IDs in use: master catalogue `zimmermann-catalog`, storefront catalogues `zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog`, pricebooks `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`), inventory list `inventory_m_au`.
- **Interim (now).** Sample data is **created manually in Business Manager** by platform, because there is no AP21-to-SFCC integration yet. Additional sample data is also manual.
- **Permanent.** Product and catalogue land via the **AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC** feed. Price lands as file-based **Pricebook XML from AP21** (there is no pricebook write API, so price is always file-based); the exact delivery path (SFTP, API, or MuleSoft) is not yet confirmed (TSD Price, open item). Building this feed is SFCC-121's scope.

*Loading-mechanism sources: Confluence Business Manager Configuration Management (309657601) and the Catalogue Sync pages (312508418, 315490342). Whether a documented `data/sample` bulk-import set exists for the sandbox is unconfirmed (open item).*

---

## 5. Limitations and gaps (Task 3)

To be covered by AP21/MuleSoft (SFCC-121) or platform:

- **Data breadth.** The dev seed is a manually-created sample set, not the full catalogue, so it is not yet at production scale for faceting or large-listing tests. Filling it out remains manual until the feed exists.
- **Product attributes not final.** The attribute model is still under discussion (per Victor); attribute-bound PDP/PLP work may need rework.
- **Sale-pricebook path unexercised.** Discount display is verified via a **promotion**; the sale-pricebook ("was/now") path is a separate mechanism and has not been tested. (The sale strategy, promotion vs sale pricebook, is itself an open item in TSD Price.)
- **Other sites and tiers unconfirmed.** Only `ZimmermannAU` on dev is verified; other storefronts and non-dev tiers are not checked.
- **Permanent feed pending.** The AP21 data feed to SFCC is not built; SFCC-121 (Validate MuleSoft Sync Process) is In Progress.

---

## 6. Permanent vs workaround (Task 4)

| Element | Classification |
|---|---|
| SCAPI-via-MRT for product/category/pricing consumption | **Permanent** (the storefront's supported model; no code change needed) |
| SLAS private-client auth via MRT | **Permanent** |
| AP21 data feed to SFCC (catalogue via MuleSoft; price as file-based Pricebook XML, delivery path TBC) | **Permanent** (data population; not yet built) |
| Manual Business Manager creation of sample data | **Workaround** (interim only; throwaway once the feed delivers) |
| OCAPI via MRT | Configured fallback; currently unused |

---

SFCC-122 "Spike: Document SFCC MRT API Capabilities" — Jira Spike, project SFCC (zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net), label Squad-A, **Code Review** (as of 2026-07-27), assignee Marcel/Angelo, reporter Jasmijn Tsang, parent epic **SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments** (owned by Mani = Manikandan Ramachandran). Siblings: SFCC-121 (Spike: Validate MuleSoft Sync Process, Victor Crisostomo, **In Progress**, parent SFCC-4 Product Catalogue), SFCC-123 (Contentful, Jhoan). Ticket asks (verified from JIRA): 4 tasks — (1) document MRT APIs endpoint/payload/auth/data, (2) assess which serve product/category/pricing in lower envs, (3) limitations/gaps for MuleSoft, (4) permanent vs workaround — plus DoD "documented inventory produced AND shared with squad, sufficient to unblock BM config + FE dev."

**Crux finding:** "MRT API" for product/category/pricing = **SCAPI Shopper APIs** (shopper-products v1 `/product/shopper-products/v1/*`, shopper-search v1 `/search/shopper-search/v1/*`, SLAS `/shopper/auth/v1/*`) reached through the MRT proxy `/mobify/proxy/api` (Dev shortCode qmyt7hks, org f_ecom_bkzk_002, site ZimmermannAU), consumed out-of-the-box via @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react hooks + the @salesforce/retail-react-app 10.0.0 template, SLAS private-client auth (ssr.js:52). The separate **Managed Runtime Admin API** (mrt-admin, platform/CI-CD) is out of scope. SCAPI is fully capable NOW; the only gap was DATA (no AP21→SFCC feed built yet). Dev bkzk-002 verified (23-24 Jul): categories via getCategory, product-search, product 4673TS251 priced 625 AUD via pricebook au-aud-list-prices, inventory_m_au ats 10, promo-driven strikethrough A$625→A$562.50 (productPromotions.promotionalPrice at variant level, NOT a sale pricebook). Price is ALWAYS file-based Pricebook XML — there is NO pricebook write API; delivery path (SFTP/API/MuleSoft) is TBC per TSD Price 292388871 §5 + open item (corroborated by Catalogue Sync 315490342 "no SCAPI Admin API for pricebook writes"). Catalogue via AP21→MuleSoft→SFCC. Catalogue IDs zimmermann-catalog + zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog; pricebooks {site}-{currency}-list/sale-prices; data/core pricebooks+inventory = empty shells (structure only) per BM Config 309657601. 4673TS251 is a colour+size variation master (per 315490342).

**DELIVERABLE STATUS (2026-07-27, CURRENT):** Reshaped from a TSD-template doc into a LEAN SPIKE-FINDINGS / INVENTORY doc after Mani's review (the TSD format "looked like just explaining PWA impl / consolidated tech details" and overlapped the existing TSD-PWA 256835585; a spike needs findings, not a problem/options/decision TSD). **PUBLISHED** to Confluence page **349437965** (now **v15**), title **"[DRAFT] SFCC MRT API Capabilities: Spike Findings (SFCC-122)"** (dropped "TSD"), under 05.1, `draft` label + DRAFT banner still ON. Structure: §1 Summary, §2 MRT API inventory (Task1), §3 What can serve now (Task2, verified table), §4 Data state & how populated, §5 Limitations (Task3), §6 Permanent vs workaround (Task4), References, Changelog. Working copy: `~/Desktop/SFCC-122-MRT-API-Capabilities.md`. Audited recursively against codebase/Confluence/JIRA: fixed SLAS path to `/shopper/auth/v1/*` (actual code slasTokens.ts:77 beats the loose `/checkout/shopper-login/*` in 01-sfcc.md), SFCC-121 status → In Progress, price-feed delivery → TBC, removed the old §7 Open Items (duplicated §5). 0 em/en dashes. Content FULLY covers all 4 tasks + Objective + both DoD unblock halves; the ONLY outstanding DoD clause is **"shared with the squad"** = outward publish/announce/link-on-ticket — page is DRAFT, NOT yet linked on SFCC-122, NOT announced (pending Angelo's go-ahead). NB the Confluence connector bumps page version ~+3 per logical update (v12→v15 here), not multiple edits.

**Deliberately EXCLUDED:** 500s observed on some product-search/getProduct calls in a 2026-07-27 dev run (likely malformed manual sample data) were NOT added — they are a data-state defect, not an MRT API capability, so out of the inventory's scope (raise to Victor separately if actioned). The old "1 sample / total:1" characterisation is stale — Victor added more products with varied configs; doc now says "manually-created sample set, varied configurations" with no specific counts. A multi-colour/option product does not change the inventory: same endpoints + `expand=variations`/`allVariationProperties`.

Key sources: codebase `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` (SCAPI endpoint inventory), `03-mulesoft.md` (PWA-direct MuleSoft = orders/returns/boutique-stock only, NOT product/price), `config/default.js`, `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`, `ssr.js`, `ssr/slasTokens.ts`. Confluence SFCC: 309657601 (BM Config), 292061208 (TSD Product), 292388871 (TSD Price), 312508418 + 315490342 (Catalogue Sync), 256835585 (TSD PWA). To finalise: remove DRAFT markers (banner + `[DRAFT]` title + `draft` label), get any required sign-off, link on SFCC-122, announce to Squad-A. See [[tsd-scope-principle]].

# SFCC-122 Spike: Learning Notes

*A study companion to the work behind the "SFCC MRT API Capabilities" spike. Written for Angelo (FED Lead) to internalise the domain knowledge, the method, and the judgement calls, so the next spike is faster and more your own.*

**Related artefacts:** published doc [Confluence 349437965](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/349437965) · ticket SFCC-122 · working copy `~/Desktop/SFCC-122-MRT-API-Capabilities.md`

---

## 0. How to use this doc

Read Part A to understand the *platform*. Read Parts B and C to understand *how to run a spike and not get fooled* (including by your AI assistant). Part D is a quick-reference cheat sheet. Part E is the honest "still open" list. If you only read one thing, read the Key Takeaways at the end.

---

## 1. What the task actually was

SFCC-122 is a **spike** (a time-boxed investigation, not a build). The ask, in plain terms:

> "Before the AP21/MuleSoft data feed exists, tell the squad which SFCC APIs are available through Managed Runtime to serve product, category, and pricing, so we can build and test in the lower environments now."

Its Definition of Done was a **documented inventory of the relevant APIs**, sufficient to unblock Business Manager config and front-end dev. Keep that phrase in mind: *documented inventory*. It dictates the shape of the deliverable (see Part B).

---

## Part A: The platform knowledge (what you now understand)

### A1. The single most important mental model

> **The API was never the blocker. Data was.**

At the start it looked like "we can't build because the APIs aren't ready." The truth: the APIs (SCAPI) are fully capable today; the storefront consumes them out of the box. What was missing was **data in the SFCC instance**, because the AP21 to SFCC feed is not built yet. Everything else in this spike hangs off that one correction.

### A2. What "MRT" is (and what it is not)

**Managed Runtime (MRT)** is the **hosting and proxy layer** for the PWA Kit storefront. It is *not* the thing that serves product/price data. Two distinct meanings hide under "MRT API," and conflating them causes confusion:

| Term | What it is | In scope for this spike? |
|---|---|---|
| **MRT (the proxy)** | Routes storefront calls (`/mobify/proxy/api`) to SFCC and handles SSR, edge, env vars | Yes, as the pathway |
| **MRT Admin API** (`mrt-admin`) | A real REST API for platform / CI-CD: environments, bundles, deploys, redirects, certs | **No** (platform, not commerce data) |
| **SCAPI Shopper APIs** | The actual commerce-data APIs (products, search, pricing) reached *through* the MRT proxy | **Yes, this is the answer** |

**Gotcha I got wrong first:** I initially claimed "MRT is not an API." That is false; the MRT Admin API exists. The right framing is the table above. *Lesson: when you assert what a platform does or does not have, check the vendor's own docs.*

### A3. How the storefront actually gets product/category/pricing

```
PWA (React, retail-react-app template)
   │  commerce-sdk-react hooks: useProduct, useProductSearch, useCategory
   ▼
MRT proxy  /mobify/proxy/api   (base host {shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com)
   ▼
SCAPI Shopper APIs
   ├─ Shopper Products   /product/shopper-products/v1/*   → product detail, price, category tree (getCategory)
   ├─ Shopper Search     /search/shopper-search/v1/*      → category listing (cgid), search, faceting
   └─ Shopper Login/SLAS /shopper/auth/v1/*               → guest + registered auth (enables every read)
```

Key facts you should be able to recite:
- Auth is **SLAS private-client** (`useSLASPrivateClient: true` in `ssr.js`); the client secret stays server-side.
- The storefront fetches related data in one call using **`expand`** (e.g. `expand=prices,promotions,variations,images`) and **`perPricebook=true`**.
- None of this is custom code. The `commerce-sdk-react` hooks and the `retail-react-app` template provide it out of the box. That is *why* "consumption is not the blocker."

### A4. Pricing: pricebooks, and two ways to show a discount

- Prices live in **pricebooks**, named **`{site}-{currency}-list-prices`** and **`-sale-prices`** (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`). Per-site, per-currency; 68 pricebooks across 8 sites.
- **There is no API to write prices.** Price is always loaded as **file-based Pricebook XML**. Remember this: it shapes how the permanent feed must work.
- A struck-through / discounted price can come from **two different mechanisms**, and they are not the same thing:
  1. **A promotion** (`productPromotions.promotionalPrice`, resolved at the *variant* level) — this is what we verified in dev (A$625 struck, A$562.50 shown).
  2. **A sale pricebook** ("was/now") — a separate mechanism we did **not** exercise.
  *Lesson: "the strikethrough works" is only true for the path you actually tested. Name the path.*

### A5. How data gets into SFCC (the data flow)

| Phase | Catalogue / product | Price |
|---|---|---|
| **Interim (now)** | Manually created in Business Manager | Manually created in BM |
| **Permanent** | AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC | AP21 → SFCC as file-based Pricebook XML (delivery path SFTP / API / MuleSoft is **TBC**) |

`data/core` in the repo holds the **structure** (catalogue IDs, pricebook shells, inventory shells) but the pricebooks/inventory are **empty shells** — the actual values come from the feed (or, for now, manual entry). That is why dev can have the pricebook `au-aud-list-prices` defined yet need someone to hand-enter the 625.

### A6. Variation products (the colour/size question)

A product with multiple colours/sizes is a **variation master** with `variationAttributes` (the axes) and `variants` (the SKUs). It uses the *same* endpoints plus `expand=variations` / `allVariationProperties=true`. More options is more *data through the same API surface*, not a new capability. The verified example `4673TS251` is itself a colour+size master (`color=GVSCP "Guava Seascape"`, `size=0P`).

### A7. What is deliberately out of scope

Baskets, orders, customers/wishlist, Shopper Context, Einstein, OCAPI (configured but unused), MuleSoft direct reads (those serve orders/returns/boutique-stock, not product/price), and the MRT Admin API. Knowing what to *exclude* is half of a good inventory.

---

## Part B: How to run a spike well (method)

### B1. Match the deliverable to what the ticket asks

This is the biggest lesson of the whole exercise. We first built a full **TSD** (Problem / Constraints / Options / Recommendation / Decision Record). Mani's reaction: it "looked like just explaining PWA impl / consolidated tech details." He was right, because:

- A **spike** asks for **findings / an inventory**. Its DoD said "documented inventory," not "a TSD."
- A **TSD** is a *decision* document for one problem with options and a recommendation. Wrapping a spike in that template pulls in scaffolding and implementation narrative that (a) the ticket never asked for and (b) overlapped the existing "TSD: PWA" page.

We reshaped it into a lean findings doc mapped 1:1 to the four tasks. It dropped ~70% of the word count and read as what it was.

> **Transferable rule:** read the DoD literally and pick the document *genre* it implies. Spike → findings/inventory. New capability with trade-offs → TSD. Bug → RCA. Do not default to the heaviest template.

### B2. One problem, and document capability not noise

A good inventory documents **what the API can do**, not every observation about one environment at one moment. This is the discipline behind the "500s" call (see C6): a 500 from the current dev seed is a *data-state* fact, not an *API-capability* fact, so it does not belong in a capabilities inventory.

### B3. Verify with source, and cite it

Every load-bearing claim should trace to a primary source: the codebase, the official docs, Confluence, or JIRA — not memory, not inference. We added inline citations so a reader can check each fact. When two sources disagree, prefer the **most authoritative** one and say so (see C2 and C5).

### B4. Recursive verification actually finds bugs

The method: **plan → verify against source → fix → re-verify → repeat until clean.** It is not ceremony. Each pass in this spike caught a real defect the previous pass missed (a wrong endpoint path, a stale ticket status, a mis-stated data-flow, then two residual inconsistencies from the fixes themselves). *Fixes introduce new inconsistencies; always re-verify after fixing.*

### B5. Traceability: "fully, and no less" (and no more)

Before calling it done, map **every ticket requirement to a section** and every section back to a requirement. That is how you can honestly say "fully fulfils the ask" and also "nothing bolted on." For SFCC-122 the only unmet DoD clause was "shared with the squad" — a *process* step (publish + review), not a content gap.

---

## Part C: The mistakes, and how they were caught (the richest learning)

Each of these is a pattern you will meet again.

| # | What went wrong | How it was caught | The lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | "MRT is not an API" (flatly wrong) | Reading the official MRT docs | Verify platform claims against the vendor's primary docs, not intuition |
| C2 | SLAS path documented as `/checkout/shopper-login/*` | The repo's *own* integration doc had it wrong; the actual runtime code (`slasTokens.ts:77`) used `/shopper/auth/v1/*` | **Runtime code beats a summary doc.** Rank your sources by authority |
| C3 | Scope creep into PWA-impl + TSD scaffolding | Mani's review | Wrong genre and audience; see B1 |
| C4 | SFCC-121 status shown as "Ready for Development" | Live JIRA said "In Progress" | Statuses are **volatile**; re-fetch them at the moment of use, do not trust memory |
| C5 | Price feed stated as bypassing MuleSoft (and later, as via MuleSoft) | "TSD: Price" says no direct MuleSoft price integration and marks the delivery path **TBC** | When sources conflict, state the verified fact and flag the unknown; do not pick a side to sound decisive |
| C6 | Instinct to document the dev 500s in the inventory | Your challenge: "are they part of the documented inventory?" | **Capability vs data-state.** A runtime error from bad sample data is not an API capability fact |

*A study companion to the work behind the "SFCC MRT API Capabilities" spike. Written for Angelo (FED Lead) to internalise the domain knowledge, the method, and the judgement calls, so the next spike is faster and more your own.*

**Related artefacts:** published doc [Confluence 349437965](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/349437965) · ticket SFCC-122 · working copy `~/Desktop/SFCC-122-MRT-API-Capabilities.md`

---

## 0. How to use this doc

Read Part A to understand the *platform*. Read Parts B and C to understand *how to run a spike and not get fooled* (including by your AI assistant). Part D is a quick-reference cheat sheet. Part E is the honest "still open" list. If you only read one thing, read the Key Takeaways at the end.

---

## 1. What the task actually was

SFCC-122 is a **spike** (a time-boxed investigation, not a build). The ask, in plain terms:

> "Before the AP21/MuleSoft data feed exists, tell the squad which SFCC APIs are available through Managed Runtime to serve product, category, and pricing, so we can build and test in the lower environments now."

Its Definition of Done was a **documented inventory of the relevant APIs**, sufficient to unblock Business Manager config and front-end dev. Keep that phrase in mind: *documented inventory*. It dictates the shape of the deliverable (see Part B).

---

## Part A: The platform knowledge (what you now understand)

### A1. The single most important mental model

> **The API was never the blocker. Data was.**

At the start it looked like "we can't build because the APIs aren't ready." The truth: the APIs (SCAPI) are fully capable today; the storefront consumes them out of the box. What was missing was **data in the SFCC instance**, because the AP21 to SFCC feed is not built yet. Everything else in this spike hangs off that one correction.

### A2. What "MRT" is (and what it is not)

**Managed Runtime (MRT)** is the **hosting and proxy layer** for the PWA Kit storefront. It is *not* the thing that serves product/price data. Two distinct meanings hide under "MRT API," and conflating them causes confusion:

| Term | What it is | In scope for this spike? |
|---|---|---|
| **MRT (the proxy)** | Routes storefront calls (`/mobify/proxy/api`) to SFCC and handles SSR, edge, env vars | Yes, as the pathway |
| **MRT Admin API** (`mrt-admin`) | A real REST API for platform / CI-CD: environments, bundles, deploys, redirects, certs | **No** (platform, not commerce data) |
| **SCAPI Shopper APIs** | The actual commerce-data APIs (products, search, pricing) reached *through* the MRT proxy | **Yes, this is the answer** |

**Gotcha I got wrong first:** I initially claimed "MRT is not an API." That is false; the MRT Admin API exists. The right framing is the table above. *Lesson: when you assert what a platform does or does not have, check the vendor's own docs.*

### A3. How the storefront actually gets product/category/pricing

```
PWA (React, retail-react-app template)
   │  commerce-sdk-react hooks: useProduct, useProductSearch, useCategory
   ▼
MRT proxy  /mobify/proxy/api   (base host {shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com)
   ▼
SCAPI Shopper APIs
   ├─ Shopper Products   /product/shopper-products/v1/*   → product detail, price, category tree (getCategory)
   ├─ Shopper Search     /search/shopper-search/v1/*      → category listing (cgid), search, faceting
   └─ Shopper Login/SLAS /shopper/auth/v1/*               → guest + registered auth (enables every read)
```

Key facts you should be able to recite:
- Auth is **SLAS private-client** (`useSLASPrivateClient: true` in `ssr.js`); the client secret stays server-side.
- The storefront fetches related data in one call using **`expand`** (e.g. `expand=prices,promotions,variations,images`) and **`perPricebook=true`**.
- None of this is custom code. The `commerce-sdk-react` hooks and the `retail-react-app` template provide it out of the box. That is *why* "consumption is not the blocker."

### A4. Pricing: pricebooks, and two ways to show a discount

- Prices live in **pricebooks**, named **`{site}-{currency}-list-prices`** and **`-sale-prices`** (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`). Per-site, per-currency; 68 pricebooks across 8 sites.
- **There is no API to write prices.** Price is always loaded as **file-based Pricebook XML**. Remember this: it shapes how the permanent feed must work.
- A struck-through / discounted price can come from **two different mechanisms**, and they are not the same thing:
  1. **A promotion** (`productPromotions.promotionalPrice`, resolved at the *variant* level) — this is what we verified in dev (A$625 struck, A$562.50 shown).
  2. **A sale pricebook** ("was/now") — a separate mechanism we did **not** exercise.
  *Lesson: "the strikethrough works" is only true for the path you actually tested. Name the path.*

### A5. How data gets into SFCC (the data flow)

| Phase | Catalogue / product | Price |
|---|---|---|
| **Interim (now)** | Manually created in Business Manager | Manually created in BM |
| **Permanent** | AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC | AP21 → SFCC as file-based Pricebook XML (delivery path SFTP / API / MuleSoft is **TBC**) |

`data/core` in the repo holds the **structure** (catalogue IDs, pricebook shells, inventory shells) but the pricebooks/inventory are **empty shells** — the actual values come from the feed (or, for now, manual entry). That is why dev can have the pricebook `au-aud-list-prices` defined yet need someone to hand-enter the 625.

### A6. Variation products (the colour/size question)

A product with multiple colours/sizes is a **variation master** with `variationAttributes` (the axes) and `variants` (the SKUs). It uses the *same* endpoints plus `expand=variations` / `allVariationProperties=true`. More options is more *data through the same API surface*, not a new capability. The verified example `4673TS251` is itself a colour+size master (`color=GVSCP "Guava Seascape"`, `size=0P`).

### A7. What is deliberately out of scope

Baskets, orders, customers/wishlist, Shopper Context, Einstein, OCAPI (configured but unused), MuleSoft direct reads (those serve orders/returns/boutique-stock, not product/price), and the MRT Admin API. Knowing what to *exclude* is half of a good inventory.

5	> **The deal:** simplified, not dumbed down. Where I use a real name (MuleSoft, NewStore…), I
6	> explain it in normal words the first time.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## The big picture, as a shop
11	
12	Picture our online store as a physical shop with a back office:
13	
14	- **The front counter = SFCC.** Where the customer browses and pays. This is *our* world (the PWA).
15	- **The dispatcher/translator in the middle = MuleSoft.** It doesn't sell anything or fulfil
16	  anything. It just carries messages between the front counter and the back office, and translates
17	  so everyone understands each other. The front counter **never talks to the back office directly** —
18	  it always goes through the dispatcher.
19	- **The back office / warehouse boss = NewStore.** This is the "OMS" (Order Management System). It
20	  actually fulfils orders, tracks their status, and **keeps the master record of every order** — both
21	  online *and* in-store. It's the source of truth for "what happened to this order."
22	
23	A few other desks in the back office you'll hear named:
24	- **AP21** — head office that decides what products exist, their prices, and stock levels.
25	- **Narvar** — the "track your parcel / start a return" desk for **local** orders.
26	- **Global-e** — same idea but for **international** orders (it also runs their checkout).
27	- **Omneo** — the loyalty/membership desk. (Not where order history comes from — remember that.)
28	
29	---
30	
31	## The one thing to really get: there are TWO roads, not one
32	
33	"Order management through MuleSoft" is actually **two totally separate jobs**. Mixing them up is the
34	easiest way to get confused in the meeting.
35	
36	**Road 1 — Sending a new order out** ("here's a fresh order, go fulfil it")
37	Customer pays → front counter tells the dispatcher "order 123 is placed" → dispatcher grabs the full
38	order details and hands them to the warehouse boss.
39	➡️ **Not our job to build in the app.** This lives in the back-end plumbing.
40	
41	**Road 2 — Asking about existing orders** ("show me my orders / where's my stuff / my returns")
42	Customer opens "My Account" → the app asks the dispatcher → dispatcher asks the warehouse boss →
43	answer comes back → we show it.
44	➡️ **This IS our job. And right now it's stuck.** This is what to focus the meeting on.
45	
46	---
47	
48	## Why Road 2 is stuck (the stuff worth asking about)
49	
50	**1. The dispatcher only knows how to talk to the OLD shop.**
51	Our dispatcher (MuleSoft) has spent years talking to our previous shop system (Magento). We're the
52	new shop (SFCC). All the "phone numbers" it uses are still labelled for the old shop. We need to know:
53	what are *our* phone numbers, and when do we get them?
54	
55	**2. The biggest blocker: we don't know the customer's "name tag."**
56	When the app asks "show me *this* customer's orders," the warehouse needs a specific ID to know who we
57	mean. **Nobody has confirmed what that ID is or where our app gets it from.** Until that's nailed
58	down, "My Orders" literally can't work — the warehouse just says "who?"
59	
60	**3. There are three different "order numbers" floating around.**
61	One number the customer sees at checkout, one the warehouse invents for itself, and one it shows in
62	order history. They're all real, but they're *different*, and the docs mix them up. We need one clear
63	picture of which number to save and which to show — otherwise clicking an order to see details breaks.
64	
65	**4. Nobody's written the "oops" plan.**
66	What happens if the customer pays, but the "new order" message never reaches the warehouse? That's the
67	scariest case — money taken, order lost. The plan for catching and retrying that doesn't exist yet for
68	our new shop. We must ask for it.
69	
70	**5. Buffer stock — who does the maths?**
71	We hold back a little stock so we don't oversell ("buffer"). Today the *old shop* did that maths.
72	For the new shop, it's unclear whether the dispatcher does it before sending us numbers, or we do it.
73	If nobody does it, we oversell.
74	
75	---
76

80	basically **nothing** yet: one empty placeholder and no real wiring. And that's fine — this work is
81	scheduled for later (Order Management ≈ Sprint 5, Returns ≈ Sprint 7). The point of the meeting is to
82	**lock down the agreement now, before we start building**, so we're not guessing later.
83	
84	⚠️ A trap that comes with this: a lot of "confirmed" answers in the docs are confirmed about the
85	**old shop (Magento)**. Just because it's true for the old shop doesn't mean it's true for us. Always

> **Who this is for:** me (FED lead) — a clear, low-jargon explanation I can actually retain.
> **What it's from:** prepping for the MuleSoft Order Management walkthrough (22 Jul 2026).
> **The deal:** simplified, not dumbed down. Where I use a real name (MuleSoft, NewStore…), I
> explain it in normal words the first time.

---

## The big picture, as a shop

Picture our online store as a physical shop with a back office:

- **The front counter = SFCC.** Where the customer browses and pays. This is *our* world (the PWA).
- **The dispatcher/translator in the middle = MuleSoft.** It doesn't sell anything or fulfil
  anything. It just carries messages between the front counter and the back office, and translates
  so everyone understands each other. The front counter **never talks to the back office directly** —
  it always goes through the dispatcher.
- **The back office / warehouse boss = NewStore.** This is the "OMS" (Order Management System). It
  actually fulfils orders, tracks their status, and **keeps the master record of every order** — both
  online *and* in-store. It's the source of truth for "what happened to this order."

A few other desks in the back office you'll hear named:
- **AP21** — head office that decides what products exist, their prices, and stock levels.
- **Narvar** — the "track your parcel / start a return" desk for **local** orders.
- **Global-e** — same idea but for **international** orders (it also runs their checkout).
- **Omneo** — the loyalty/membership desk. (Not where order history comes from — remember that.)

---

## The one thing to really get: there are TWO roads, not one

"Order management through MuleSoft" is actually **two totally separate jobs**. Mixing them up is the
easiest way to get confused in the meeting.

**Road 1 — Sending a new order out** ("here's a fresh order, go fulfil it")
Customer pays → front counter tells the dispatcher "order 123 is placed" → dispatcher grabs the full
order details and hands them to the warehouse boss.
➡️ **Not our job to build in the app.** This lives in the back-end plumbing.

**Road 2 — Asking about existing orders** ("show me my orders / where's my stuff / my returns")
Customer opens "My Account" → the app asks the dispatcher → dispatcher asks the warehouse boss →
answer comes back → we show it.
➡️ **This IS our job. And right now it's stuck.** This is what to focus the meeting on.

---

## Why Road 2 is stuck (the stuff worth asking about)

**1. The dispatcher only knows how to talk to the OLD shop.**
Our dispatcher (MuleSoft) has spent years talking to our previous shop system (Magento). We're the
new shop (SFCC). All the "phone numbers" it uses are still labelled for the old shop. We need to know:
what are *our* phone numbers, and when do we get them?

**2. The biggest blocker: we don't know the customer's "name tag."**
When the app asks "show me *this* customer's orders," the warehouse needs a specific ID to know who we
mean. **Nobody has confirmed what that ID is or where our app gets it from.** Until that's nailed
down, "My Orders" literally can't work — the warehouse just says "who?"

**3. There are three different "order numbers" floating around.**
One number the customer sees at checkout, one the warehouse invents for itself, and one it shows in
order history. They're all real, but they're *different*, and the docs mix them up. We need one clear
picture of which number to save and which to show — otherwise clicking an order to see details breaks.

**4. Nobody's written the "oops" plan.**
What happens if the customer pays, but the "new order" message never reaches the warehouse? That's the
scariest case — money taken, order lost. The plan for catching and retrying that doesn't exist yet for
our new shop. We must ask for it.

**5. Buffer stock — who does the maths?**
We hold back a little stock so we don't oversell ("buffer"). Today the *old shop* did that maths.
For the new shop, it's unclear whether the dispatcher does it before sending us numbers, or we do it.
If nobody does it, we oversell.

---

## The other big realisation: it's all designed, almost none of it is built

There's a *lot* of documentation — designs, requirements, diagrams. But in the actual code, there's
basically **nothing** yet: one empty placeholder and no real wiring. And that's fine — this work is
scheduled for later (Order Management ≈ Sprint 5, Returns ≈ Sprint 7). The point of the meeting is to
**lock down the agreement now, before we start building**, so we're not guessing later.

⚠️ A trap that comes with this: a lot of "confirmed" answers in the docs are confirmed about the
**old shop (Magento)**. Just because it's true for the old shop doesn't mean it's true for us. Always
ask: *"is that answer about the old system or the new one?"*

---

## How I actually figured all this out (the method — reusable)

This is the part worth keeping as a skill, because you'll do it again for the next integration:

1. **Split the topic first.** "One meeting title" hid two separate jobs (send-out vs ask-about).
   Spotting that early made everything clearer.
2. **Look in three places at once:** the code (what's *really* built), Confluence (the *design*), and
   Jira (the *plan and open decisions*). They rarely agree — and the disagreements are the gold.
3. **Sort everything into "already answered" vs "still open."** Don't waste a vendor's time asking
   what's already settled — it makes you look unprepared.
4. **Hunt for contradictions.** The single most useful output was finding **6 places where two docs
   say different things** about the same fact. Each one becomes a "we must clarify this" question.
5. **Rank by "does this stop us building?"** Blockers first, nice-to-knows last.
6. **Shape the write-up for whoever reads it.** The version for the vendor got a plain intro, a
   "why we're asking" under each question, and a blank line for them to answer.

---

## Gut-check questions (if I can answer these, I get it)

1. In one sentence each: what does the front counter (SFCC), the dispatcher (MuleSoft), and the
   warehouse boss (NewStore) each do?
2. What are the two "roads," and which one is our job to build in the app?
3. Why can't "My Orders" work yet, even though the endpoint supposedly exists?
4. Why is a fact that's "confirmed" in the docs sometimes still risky for us?
5. What's the scariest failure in placing an order, and why does it matter most?

---

## What happens next (after the meeting)

- Get the answers to the blockers above written down, especially the **customer "name tag"** and the
  **new phone numbers (endpoints)**.
- Record the vendor's answers back in the shared Open Questions page, and update the relevant tickets.
- Fix the contradictions at the source so the next person doesn't trip over them.

---

*Deeper, more technical version of this same learning lives in the repo at
`.docs/learning/mulesoft-order-management.md`. The vendor question list is in
`~/Downloads/mulesoft-order-management-questions.md`.*

1	# Breaking a big user story into small ones — the plain-English version
2	
3	> **Who this is for:** me (FED lead) — the clear, low-jargon version I can actually retain.
4	> **What it's from:** Jas (our BA) asked how to split `SFCC-195`, the PDP "Product Information
5	> Accordion" (those expandable tabs on the product page). Tim's been pushing everyone to write
6	> smaller, "one-component-at-a-time" stories. This is what I took away.
7	> **The deal:** simplified, not dumbed down. Where I use a real name (Contentful, AP21…), I explain
8	> it in normal words the first time. Glossary at the bottom.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## The one thing to really get
13	
14	Picture the accordion as a **filing cabinet**, and each tab as a **drawer**:
15	
16	> Details & Care · Size & Fit · Shipping & Returns · Assistance · Environmental Qualities
17	
18	Jas's first idea: **one ticket per drawer.** Feels tidy.
19	
20	Here's the catch — **all the drawers look the same** (a label, and some text that opens up). The thing that's actually *different* is **where the paper inside each drawer comes from**:
21	
22	- **Details & Care, Size & Fit** → from the **product record** (info stored on the product itself)
23	- **Shipping & Returns, Assistance** → from **Contentful** (the tool the content team edits without a developer)
24	- **Environmental Qualities** → from **AP21** (the product data system), EU shops only
25	
26	So the smart cut isn't "one ticket per drawer." It's **"group the drawers by where their paper comes from."**
27	
28	➡️ **The lesson in one line: split by where the content comes from, not by what the shopper sees.**
29	
30	Why? Because the real work is building the *pipe* that fetches each kind of paper. Two drawers fed by the same pipe = the same work = one ticket. Splitting them into two tickets just means building the same pipe twice.
31	
32	That took Jas's 6 tickets down to about 4, cut along the pipes instead of the drawers.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Lesson 1 — a ticket should be something you can actually show
37	
38	Jas's plan started with a "just the empty cabinet, no drawers" ticket. Problem: **you can't demo an empty cabinet.** Nobody can look at it and go "yep, that works."
39	
40	Fix: **put one real drawer inside the cabinet ticket** so there's something to see and tick off.
41	
42	➡️ Rule of thumb: every ticket should be a thin but *whole* strip — something a person can look at and sign off — never a hidden layer no one can see.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## Lesson 2 — we've done this before, so copy the pattern (don't invent one)
47	
48	When Tim says "component-based stories," he's describing something the team **already did** on the filters work:
49	- one ticket to build the shared piece once,
50	- one ticket to plug it into each page.
51	
52	(For the record: `SFCC-108` built the shared filter component, `SFCC-199` plugged it into the listing page. "Recently Viewed," `SFCC-83`, did the same.)
53	
54	➡️ Lesson for me as lead: my proposals get an easy "yes" when I say *"this is the same shape as the filters work"* instead of inventing a new approach. Point at the last time we did it.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Lesson 3 — split again when one drawer is riskier than another
59	
60	Details & Care and Size & Fit both come from the product record — so by my own rule, that's one ticket. **But** Size & Fit needs a **new bit of product info that doesn't exist yet** (someone still has to confirm it with the business). Details & Care uses info we already have.
61	
62	So I kept them apart. If I bundle them, the safe one gets stuck waiting on the unsure one.
63	
64	➡️ Rule of thumb: same source = group them. But if one piece is **waiting on an unknown** (info not confirmed, content not written, a tool not built) — split it off so it doesn't drag the rest down.
65	
66	---
67	
68	## Lesson 4 — don't drag in something another team is building later; let it wait politely
69	
70	The "Assistance" drawer *looked* like it might be special. It has email, phone, opening hours, WhatsApp, a contact link… and a **"Start a Chat"** button.
71	
72	Everything except the chat button is just text and links — same as the Shipping & Returns drawer. The chat button is the only real difference, because it opens the **live chat widget**, and that widget:
73	- can't switch on until the shopper accepts cookies,
74	- decides its own "are we online right now" behaviour,
75	- and is being built by **another team, in a later sprint** — it doesn't exist yet.
76	
77	We have a written rule: **don't build against something from a later sprint.**
78	
79	So the move was: **build the drawer now, but make the chat button harmless until the widget shows up.** If the chat's there, the button opens it; if not, it just sits quietly. Wire it up properly later, when the other team's part lands.
80	
81	➡️ End result: Assistance stayed in **one** ticket with Shipping & Returns, and the chat button became a small "come back to this later" note tied to the other team's work. Nothing got blocked.
82	
83	(The proper name for "still works, just quietly does less, when a piece is missing" is *graceful degradation*. Worth knowing — it's often the trick that lets you keep one ticket instead of splitting or blocking.)
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Lesson 5 — if the ticket assumes something the spec hasn't decided, say so
88	
89	The ticket confidently said "these drawers come from Contentful, those from the product record." But our actual spec (the PRD) **still lists that exact decision as "not decided yet."**
90	
91	I flagged it — politely — because the whole split leans on that decision. If it changes later, the split falls apart.
92	
93	➡️ Lesson: before I build a plan on a "fact," I check the spec. If the ticket is running ahead of the spec, I raise it instead of quietly assuming.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## Lesson 6 — talk to a BA in BA language
98	
99	In my head this was all "fetch, sanitise, cookie-gate, degrade." What I actually **sent Jas** was: how many tickets, what's bundled, what's a dependency, which team/sprint owns what, and what keeps us unblocked.
100	
101	I also said out loud where **her** idea was better (more tickets = easier to track progress and hand out to different people), so it felt like we decided together — not like I overruled her.
102	
103	➡️ Lesson: do the deep thinking for myself; send the plain, scope-and-dependencies version to them. And always name the trade-offs of their idea — it builds trust and gets to "yes" faster.
104	
105	---
106	
107	## My quick checklist (steal this next time)
108	
109	1. **Read everything first** — the ticket, the spec bit it points to, and check whether the thing even exists in our code yet.
110	2. For each part, ask **"where does its content come from?"** and group the parts that share a source.
111	3. **Split again** wherever one part is waiting on an unknown.
112	4. Make every ticket **demoable** — give the "shell" ticket one real drawer.
113	5. Anything **another team / later sprint owns** → don't pull it in; build it to sit quietly until their part lands.
114	6. **Point at the last time we split something the same way** — makes the "yes" easy.
115	7. If the ticket assumes something the spec hasn't settled, **flag it.**
116	8. Someone wants more tickets just for tracking? Use **sub-tasks**, not extra stories.
117	9. Write the reply in **their** language, and name where their idea wins.
118	
119	---
120	
121	## Words I used (so they stop being scary)
122	
123	- **Vertical slice / walking skeleton** — a thin but *complete* piece you can actually show and tick off. Opposite: an invisible layer no one can see.
124	- **Data source** — where a piece of content actually comes from (our product system vs the content tool vs AP21).
125	- **Dependency** — something this work needs that lives elsewhere (another ticket, team, or sprint).
126	- **Graceful degradation** — building it so it still works, just quietly does less, when a piece it wants isn't ready yet.
127	- **Cookie-gated / consent-gated** — can't switch on until the shopper accepts cookies.
128	- **Contentful** — the content tool the marketing/content team edits without needing a developer.
129	- **AP21** — the product data system a lot of our product info comes from.
130	- **PRD** — the spec / "what we agreed to build" document. Source of truth for requirements.
131	- **Sprint / squad** — a sprint is a ~2-week chunk of work; a squad is one of our two teams. "Later sprint / other squad" = not our job right now.
132	- **Sub-task vs story** — a story is a standalone chunk of value; a sub-task is a checklist item *inside* a story. Use sub-tasks when you want finer tracking without more standalone tickets.
133	
134	---
135	
136	## Still to do
137	- Write the "chat button hooks up later" note somewhere it won't get lost (on the ticket + linked to the chat-widget work).
138	- Chase the "where does the content come from" decision so it's actually confirmed.
139	- Confirm the new Size & Fit product info with the business.
140	- Make sure I don't end up building the product-page structure twice across my own tickets.
141	
142	---
